correctness.rationale: The lower bound of twenty comes from sixteen RC pairs requiring sixteen windows. The complete sixteen-bit orientation-mask certificate enumerates all sixty-five thousand five hundred thirty-six selected-edge systems: fifty-two balanced, eighteen strongly connected, whose distinguished-edge Euler tour counts are eight of one, eight of two and two of four, totaling 32 cycles. An exact vertex-imbalance argument proves all shortest binary odd-order covers close; every order-five cycle has period sixteen, yielding exactly 512 rooted linear words. The eight four-element complement/reversal symmetry orbits are listed. Included verify.cpp independently exhausts all 1,048,576 literal length-twenty words and replays the orientation certificate, with exact matching recorded output. No finite check is used to justify an unproved all-order count.

originality.rationale: The relevant full-text 2013 RC-complete-sequences theorem proves the optimal odd-order length and poses counting all optimizers as an open question (section 5), but does not enumerate binary order-five words. Full-text Chang–Wang 2024 exhibits one 16-cycle identical to a representative and proves the number of complementary-reverse full de Bruijn sequences is divisible by a power of two, not the exact count of shortest 16-class half-cycles. The 2026 SCS-RC paper studies approximation algorithms rather than this equality-case census. Searches of published scientific records and the accessible prior scientific claims found no exact 512/32/eight-class theorem. A previously unindexed or indirectly equivalent earlier count remains possible.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed table or enumeration could already establish the binary five-mer count and eight orbits.

A reduction from a stronger published exact count of full complement-reverse de Bruijn sequences could potentially cover this half-cycle census without identical terminology; no such decisive theorem was found in the inspected full text.

value.rationale: The count of different shortest RC-complete sequences is an explicitly articulated enumerative research gap in Orenstein–Shamir (2013); knowing one optimum or the length alone does not address it. The binary five-mer model gives the first interesting small odd-order full equality-case classification with eight genuine reversal/complement symmetry types and a separate general forced-closure lemma. It supplies a natural exact benchmark for strand-unoriented sequence coverage, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
